data.claim: git patch-id --stable of a cherry-picked commit equals the original's, so scanning main for an equal patch-id finds the rewritten equivalent
data.falsifier: a cherry-picked commit whose patch-id differs
data.mechanism: patch-id hashes the diff hunks, not commit metadata
data.question: Does a cherry-picked commit share its patch-id with the original so a rewritten recorded sha can be matched?

chunk_findings.detail: `ddflow_verify(..., shas=True)` returns before `_tool_mode_refusal`, so conflicting mode flags are dropped rather than refused. Given `shas=True`, `pack_=True`, and `id="T1"`, the function runs only `verify_shas` and never refuses the pack argument, contradicting the docstring on the same function that other-mode arguments are refused, never dropped.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/verify.py:284

chunk_findings.detail: Landed-path matching treats any newer commit whose name-only set is a superset of the recorded files as the rewrite of `sha`. Candidates are newest-first, and the first hit wins even when patch-ids differ. Given a completed item whose sha is not an ancestor of main, `done.files == ["pkg/a.py"]`, and tip `bbbb` that only fixes a typo in `pkg/a.py`, `_equivalent` returns `(bbbb, "landed paths")` and `check_item` reports `rewritten, equivalent bbbb`. That commit is not the recorded change, so a task that never landed is reported as landed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/verify_shas.py:_equivalent

chunk_findings.detail: `shas=True` returns before `_tool_mode_refusal`, so flags that the same docstring says are refused, never dropped, are silently ignored. `ddflow_verify(..., id="T1", shas=True, pack_=True, judge_=True)` runs `verify_shas` on `T1` and never refuses the pack/judge combination; `id="T1", phase="other", shas=True` likewise drops `phase` instead of refusing two targets.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/verify.py:ddflow_verify

chunk_findings.detail: Landed-path fallback treats any newer commit whose path set merely contains the recorded files as the rewritten landing. Candidates come from `git log -n400` (newest first), and the first commit where `set(landed) <= set(_paths_of(c))` is returned as `rewritten, equivalent <sha> (matched by landed paths)` even when patch-id did not match or the original object is gone. Given a completion whose sha was rebased away and `done.files == ["src/a.py"]`, a later typo fix that only touches `src/a.py` is reported as the equivalent of that task, so verify claims the work is on main under the wrong hash.

chunk_findings.detail: `cmd_verify` returns from `_shas` before `_refusal`, and `_shas` sets `target = a.id or a.phase` then calls `verify_shas` with only that string. `ddflow verify --shas T1 --phase other` therefore checks T1 and never refuses the second target; `ddflow verify --shas T1 --pack` likewise never reaches the refusal path and drops `--pack`. chunk_findings.detail: Landed-path matching treats any newer commit whose name-only set is a superset of the recorded files as the rewrite of `sha`. Candidates are newest-first, and the first hit wins even when patch-ids differ. Given a completed item whose sha is not an ancestor of main, `done.files == ["pkg/a.py"]`, and tip `bbbb` that only fixes a typo in `pkg/a.py`, `_equivalent` returns `(bbbb, "landed paths")` and `check_item` reports `rewritten, equivalent bbbb`. That commit is not the recorded change, so a task that never landed is reported as landed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/verify_shas.py:_equivalent

chunk_findings.detail: Landed-path matching still reports a later commit as the rewrite when it is not that change. After a patch-id miss the loop still returns the newest commit whose path set equals the recorded files and whose message contains the item id, with no patch-id check on that hit. Given item `T1`, `sha` present and not an ancestor, a different patch-id, `done.files == ["pkg/a.py"]`, and tip `bbbb` whose only change is a typo in `pkg/a.py` with message `T1 typo`, `_equivalent` returns `(bbbb, "landed paths")` and `check_item` reports `rewritten, equivalent bbbb`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/verify_shas.py:113

chunk_findings.detail: `item in msg.out` is a raw substring, so a different commit is accepted as the landing. Given item `T1`, recorded files `["pkg/a.py"]`, and a newer commit that touches only `pkg/a.py` with message `Merge T10`, `"T1" in "Merge T10"` is true, the path sets are equal, and `_equivalent` returns that commit as `landed paths`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/verify_shas.py:_mentions

chunk_findings.detail: A revert is treated as a landing unless the subject literally starts with "revert". Given landed files ["pkg/c.py"], item T1, and a single candidate whose subject is "fix: revert T1" (or whose body is "This reverts commit abc" while the subject is "undo T1") with exactly those paths, `_mentions_landing` is true, `len(hits)==1`, and `_equivalent` returns that commit as "landed paths". The change is reported rewritten/equivalent even though the only match undoes the work. The same prefix also drops a real landing titled "Revert the old parser for T1" when it is the unique path match, so that item is reported missing.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/verify_shas.py:_mentions_landing

chunk_findings.detail: `"revert" in subject` treats any subject that merely contains that letter sequence as an undo. Given landed files `["pkg/d.py"]`, item T1, and one candidate whose subject is `T1: make the parser change reversible` (or `T1: do not revert the parser`) and whose paths are exactly those files, `undone` is true, `_mentions_landing` returns false, and the landed-paths equivalent is dropped, so the item is reported missing even though that commit is the landing. The same happens for `irreversible`. The added test only covers a subject that actually says `revert`, so it does not catch this.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/verify_shas.py:105

chunk_findings.detail: The word-boundary check still treats a landing whose subject merely says not to revert as an undo. Given landed files `["pkg/d.py"]`, item T1, and one candidate whose subject is `T1: do not revert the parser` and whose paths are exactly those files, `\brevert(s|ed|ing)?\b` matches, `undone` is true, `_mentions_landing` returns false, and the landed-paths equivalent is dropped, so the item is reported missing. The new probe only covers `reversible`, so it does not answer that input from the confirmed finding.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/verify_shas.py:106

chunk_findings.detail: The landed-path fallback still walks `reversed(cands)` and returns the oldest commit whose path set equals `done.files` and whose subject mentions the item. Given a missing object, `done.files == ["pkg/a.py"]`, item `T1`, and history `C1` subject "T1 WIP" then `C2` "Land T1" both touching only `pkg/a.py` (and a later `Revert T1`), `_mentions_landing` drops the revert but the oldest match returns `C1` as `rewritten, equivalent`. `C1` is not the landing; a newest non-revert exact-path match would select `C2`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/verify_shas.py:_equivalent

chunk_findings.detail: `cmd_verify` returns from `_shas` before `_refusal`, and `_shas` sets `target = a.id or a.phase` then calls `verify_shas` with only that string. `ddflow verify --shas T1 --phase other` therefore checks T1 and never refuses the second target; `ddflow verify --shas T1 --pack` likewise never reaches the refusal path and drops `--pack`. That is the same silent-drop the API path was required to refuse.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/commands/verify.py:_shas

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding 4 still holds. `test_a_revert_naming_the_item_is_not_its_landing_and_the_oldest_match_wins` asserts `equivalent == first` for a missing sha whose `done.files` is `["pkg/c.py"]` when history is `T1 add c` then `Revert T1 add c`. That contract is “oldest exact-path mention wins,” so a revert is skipped only because it is newer. Given a missing object, the same files, item `T1`, and history `C1` message `T1 WIP` then `C2` message `Land T1`, both touching only `pkg/c.py`, the same rule returns `C1` as `rewritten, equivalent`. `C1` is not the landing; the revert filter never runs because the oldest match returns first. This test does not cover that input, so it does not refute the defect.

chunk_findings.detail: `cmd_verify` returns from `_shas` before `_refusal`, and `_shas` sets `target = a.id or a.phase` then calls `verify_shas` with only that string. `ddflow verify --shas T1 --phase other` therefore checks T1 and never refuses the second target; `ddflow verify --shas T1 --pack` likewise never reaches the refusal path and drops `--pack`. That is the same silent-drop the API path was required to refuse.

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding 4 still holds. `test_a_revert_naming_the_item_is_not_its_landing_and_the_oldest_match_wins` asserts `equivalent == first` for a missing sha whose `done.files` is `["pkg/c.py"]` when history is `T1 add c` then `Revert T1 add c`. That contract is “oldest exact-path mention wins,” so a revert is skipped only because it is newer. Given a missing object, the same files, item `T1`, and history `C1` message `T1 WIP` then `C2` message `Land T1`, both touching only `pkg/c.py`, the same rule returns `C1` as `rewritten, equivalent`. `C1` is not the landing; the revert filter never runs because the oldest match returns first. This test does not cover that input, so it does not refute the defect.

chunk_findings.detail: The change deletes `equivalence_note` and the only test that called it (`test_equivalence_note_names_the_twin_of_a_rewritten_sha`). The stated acceptance is that a non-ancestor sha on complete warns with the equivalence result, and that a rewritten sha is reported with its patch-id twin. After this diff, nothing in the change still produces that note: `equivalence_note(repo, old)` no longer exists, so a rewritten sha passed to complete cannot yield "an equivalent commit is <twin> (matched by …)", and the regression test that asserted `twin[:10] in VS.equivalence_note(repo, old)` is gone. The manifest lists no replacement caller or helper.
